articles.headline: Microsoft skipped OpenAI’s decision model and built its own on Alibaba’s Qwen
articles.dek: Microsoft launched Decision Foundry, a low‑cost decision‑model service that runs on Alibaba’s Qwen and is already serving trillions of tokens inside Azure.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Microsoft launched Decision Foundry, a decision‑model service built on Alibaba’s Qwen, bypassing OpenAI’s offering. The service charges $0.42 per million inputs and has already processed trillions of tokens for Microsoft’s own workloads. [FACT:7908b87503915b5cf0f4a3acffc51677] [FACT:0ee40fafc9969742ce6946bd990f1817] [FACT:7db97513b857681998a4668939f7e598] [FACT:aac7660ac520430e840bae86b659c8eb]
Why This Matters

Kubernetes teams get a native, Azure‑proximate inference endpoint that avoids OpenAI licensing fees, while keeping pricing under a dollar per hundred thousand tokens. The first customer is Microsoft itself, so the service is already hardened in production. [FACT:22848cb5dea57fdf63e6a7a4b1d5c1c3]
What Happened

On Friday Microsoft announced Decision Foundry, a single‑source model‑as‑a‑service that runs on the Qwen architecture and is already live inside Azure’s own workloads. The rollout skipped the OpenAI model entirely. [FACT:7908b87503915b5cf0f4a3acffc51677] [FACT:0ee40fafc9969742ce6946bd990f1817]
Builder View

If you use KServe, Tekton, or any HTTP‑based GPU driver, you can point it at the Decision Foundry endpoint the same way you would an OpenAI API. Pricing sits at $0.42 per million inputs, and the service lives in the same Azure region as your cluster, so latency should be comparable or better. [FACT:7db97513b857681998a4668939f7e598]
Open Questions
Microsoft is roughly three‑and‑a‑half weeks behind its internal roadmap, so the timeline for a broader public rollout remains unclear. [FACT:bfaf3cf1dc1dec9f8659697bb10f4761]
Ardur Take

Decision Foundry gives cloud‑native builders a cheaper, Azure‑integrated alternative to OpenAI’s decision model, but it’s still early – expect to run a pilot before moving critical workloads. [FACT:7908b87503915b5cf0f4a3acffc51677] [FACT:0ee40fafc9969742ce6946bd990f1817]

keyPoints: Microsoft launched Decision Foundry on Alibaba’s Qwen, sidestepping OpenAI.
Cost is $0.42 per million inputs – far cheaper than comparable OpenAI tiers.
The service is already handling trillions of tokens for internal Microsoft workloads.
articles.whyItMatters: A low‑cost, Azure‑native decision model lets Kubernetes teams add AI reasoning to their services without extra licensing, and with latency benefits from regional proximity.
articles.readerAction: Spin up a quick test in your cluster: call the Decision Foundry REST endpoint with a sample payload and compare cost and latency against your current solution.
